clue.text: Hard work put to the test by runner

parts.note: a river runs, so in crosswords a runner can be a river, here the Indus of South Asia
to put something to the test is to try it

explanation.surface: Strenuous effort is examined by an athlete on the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete but is a river, the Indus.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry in its older sense is diligence, steady hard labour.

clue.text: Untouched it can't explode

indicators.note: to explode is to blow apart, so these letters are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: A bomb left untouched can't go off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intact is whole and unharmed, never having been touched.

clue.text: Refusal in Northern Ireland to enter agreement

indicators.note: one piece is said to go into the other, which signals putting it inside

parts.note: a deal is an agreement struck between parties

explanation.surface: A negotiator in Belfast declines to join a pact.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is a refusal, of a request or of a claim.

clue.text: Appropriate for a writer of romantic fiction say

indicators.note: say signals that the writer's name is to be spoken and heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Danielle Steel is a best-selling American author of romance novels

explanation.surface: A word judged suitable for a romance novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take it without right, which is to pilfer it.

clue.text: Stirred up by nonsense about American newspaper boss

indicators.note: the rubbish is placed round the American, so about means surrounding here

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish talk
US is short for American, as in the United States
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone was riled by a US editor talking rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rousted means roused or stirred into action, routed out.

clue.text: Brooded over Doctor Who's words of contempt

indicators.note: a hen sits over its eggs, so one piece covers the other here

parts.note: a brooding hen sat on its eggs

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered in order

parts.note: the clue word Who, its possessive ending ignored, is the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone sulked over a catchphrase from the TV series Doctor Who.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' looks like the TV show; 'Doctor' is the anagram signal, making OWH from WHO, which sits inside SAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dismissive retort showing one could not care less.

clue.text: Return before the woman's informed or else

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for before is turned round

parts.note: to means before in telling the time, as in ten to six
her is the possessive meaning the woman's
wise means knowing, well informed

explanation.surface: A lady comes back early, knowing what would happen otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise and or else both introduce the alternative consequence.

clue.text: It's inherited by John after he goes to Ireland to get married

indicators.note: John comes after the earlier pieces, so his letters are placed second

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, a loo
M stands for married in genealogies and forms

explanation.surface: A man named John moves to Ireland to wed and receives a family treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a person but is slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a valued object handed down through a family.

clue.text: Speculate in article about knight breaking poet's heart

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the knight's title breaks into the poet's centre, so it goes inside
the heart of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: the clue word poet, its possessive ending ignored

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the title is read backwards

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: Wondering about a magazine piece on a knight who breaks a poet's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SIR into RIS, and 'breaking' puts that inside OE, the heart of POET, after THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to form ideas without proof, which is to speculate.

clue.text: Maybe the present head of department at college is unable to relax

parts.note: the present is one example of a grammatical tense

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: being up means being in residence at university

explanation.surface: A departmental head at a college frets over a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the present' looks like a gift, but is the present tense; the 'Maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tensed up is rigid with nerves and cannot unwind.

clue.text: Select an alternative

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, select means hand-picked, of top quality
an option one may pick among others

explanation.definitionFit: Choice as an adjective means top-grade, and as a noun means an available option.

clue.text: Against popular books being withdrawn

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the books are turned round

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone opposes popular titles being pulled from shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into or up against something are the same: into can mean in collision with.

clue.text: Girl receiving help at the outset to beat fraud

indicators.note: the girl takes in the letter, so it goes inside her name

parts.note: Carla is a girl's name

indicators.note: the outset of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A girl who gets early help to defeat a con artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a fraud who claims skills he lacks, a quack.

clue.text: King and queen accepting extremely unusual measure

indicators.note: the royal pair take in the other letters, so they go between them

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A royal couple adopt a very odd policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is a straight-edged tool used to measure lengths.

clue.text: National leader introduced to Rotten's group

indicators.note: one piece is brought into the other, so it is put inside

parts.note: rotten means bad

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter

explanation.surface: A national figurehead joins the punk singer Johnny Rotten's outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' looks like Johnny Rotten of the Sex Pistols, but just means BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of musicians playing together.

clue.text: Delightful Australian actress fed with drugs

indicators.note: the actress has the drugs put into her, so they go inside

parts.note: Betty Grable was a Hollywood actress
E is slang for ecstasy, so two of them make drugs

explanation.surface: A charming Australian actress has been given drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable means pleasant, nice to be with.

clue.text: Love without admitting old foreboding

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: minus means without

explanation.surface: Love without accepting the past brings a sense of dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous and foreboding both describe something threatening ill to come.

clue.text: With reference to one call following close of coconut shy

parts.note: re means with reference to, concerning

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to ring is to call by phone

explanation.surface: A phone call follows the end of a fairground coconut shy.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a fairground stall where balls are thrown at coconuts; 'shy' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring person is reserved and modest, shy of attention.

clue.text: Injured in blast outside Uruguay's capital city

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the other one
injured means damaged, so the letters are knocked out of order
a capital is the initial letter

explanation.surface: Someone hurt in an explosion outside Montevideo, Uruguay's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' turns IN BLAST into ISTANBL, placed 'outside' U.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is the largest city in Turkey.

clue.text: Goal nets absolutely guaranteed

indicators.note: to net is to catch, so the goal holds the other word

parts.note: an end is a goal, an aim
sure means certainly, absolutely

explanation.surface: Scoring was certain once the ball hit the back of the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goal' and 'nets' suggest football, but Goal means an end, an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensured means made certain, which is to have guaranteed it.

clue.text: Drop of scotch

definitions.meaning: a small splash of liquid added
to scotch a plan is to thwart or end it

explanation.definitionFit: A dash is a small drop of liquid, and to dash hopes is to scotch them.

clue.text: Essential to visit Henley next

indicators.note: Essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: It is vital to go to Henley, the Thames rowing regatta town, next.
explanation.definitionFit: Then means afterwards, coming in sequence after.

clue.text: Convert dismissed by crowd

parts.note: to turn something is to convert it into something else
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A convert is rejected by a mob.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnout is the number of people who attend, a crowd.

clue.text: Work to keep winning like Wolves

indicators.note: the work holds the other word, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a line is one's line of work, a trade
being up means ahead, winning

explanation.surface: A football club must keep winning to be like Wolverhampton Wanderers.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club; here it is just wolves.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupine means relating to or like a wolf, from Latin lupus.

clue.text: Well used book gets put away

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A dog-eared book is packed away.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaten track is one well trodden, worn by much use.

clue.text: How Tartuffe ends is silly

parts.note: how something ends is described as ending in a given letter, here in an

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: The way a Moliere comedy finishes is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: Tartuffe, Moliere's play, ends in an E: put the phrase IN AN E together.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means foolish and empty of sense.

clue.text: Rigorous about pursuing unionist's criticism

parts.note: strict means rigorous
U is an abbreviation for Unionist in Northern Irish politics
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Strict comments on a Unionist's harsh remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: A stricture is a severe critical remark, censure.

clue.text: Catholic king having no doubt

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A Catholic monarch is certain of his faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Being clear about something means being certain, free of doubt.

clue.text: That's to go around protective covering on Mark's neck

indicators.note: the outer letters surround the inner pieces

parts.note: ie means that is

indicators.note: the covering sits on the mark, which sends it after the letter for mark

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mark
a bib protects clothes when eating

explanation.surface: A bib is put round Mark's neck to protect it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neck' looks like body part, but is slang for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To neck a drink is to swallow it fast, to drink it down.

clue.text: James was one to snivel terribly

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so these letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: James was someone who whined awfully.
explanation.walkthrough: James is Henry James, the American author of The Portrait of a Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James was a writer of long fiction, an example of the type.

clue.text: Starts to examine tumour at the back of bird's throat

parts.note: a gull is a seabird

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A vet begins checking a growth at the back of a bird's throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the back of' places ET after GULL.
explanation.definitionFit: The gullet is the passage from mouth to stomach, the throat.

clue.text: Swimmer not sure about collecting gold at first

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the other, placing it inside
about means around, so the letters are moved round
at first means the first letter

explanation.surface: A swimmer unsure about collecting a gold medal at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges NOT SURE into STUREON, and 'collecting' puts G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturgeon is a large fish, swimming in rivers and seas.
